items.title: Connect coding agents to Fabric notebooks with FNTK (Preview)
items.excerpt: The Fabric Notebook Toolkit (Preview) helps developers shorten the feedback loop between writing code and validating it with live notebook results. It connects coding agents to Microsoft Fabric notebooks through a command-line interface (CLI) that runs in the terminal alongside tools such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, and Codex. An agent can inspect the current code, run one cell, review its output, make a targeted change, and run it again without resubmitting the entire notebook—much as a human programmer working interactively. Figure: Animated GIF A coding agent uses FNTK from the terminal to interact with a Microsoft Fabric notebook. From code suggestions to notebook execution A coding agent can help write a transformation, but a proposed change is not the same as a working result. When execution happens elsewhere, developers must move code into a notebook, run it, and bring the results or errors back to the agent. FNTK connects those steps so the agent can work with a running Fabric notebook and its execution results instead of relying only on code shared in the conversation. items.excerpt: Claude Duet is a proactive agent that works for you, even while you’re away. It builds on two layers of protection: safety training in the Claude model itself and the safeguards that exist in products like Claude Code and Claude Managed Agents. On top of those, we added new protections for working across your accounts and acting on your behalf.

items.title: Manage once, reuse everywhere: Introducing variable library support for Eventstream (Preview)
items.excerpt: Moving a real-time data pipeline from development to test to production should not mean reconfiguring every source and destination. Yet environment-specific connection details and destination references can make each release a manual, error-prone task. Variable library integration with Eventstream in Microsoft Fabric lets teams reuse the same eventstream definition across environments, with references that resolve to each environment's resources. What's new? Variable library integration with Eventstream is available in preview. For supported source connections and destination items, you can use variable library references instead of direct values. These references are preserved through Git integration and deployment pipelines, helping teams reuse an eventstream definition across workspaces with environment-specific configuration. How variable library integration works Variable library is an item type in Microsoft Fabric that provides a centralized way to define and manage configuration values at the workspace level. items.title: Bringing Rust-native Spark compatibility to Microsoft OneLake with Sail and LakeSail
items.excerpt: Coauthor: Shehab Amin Microsoft OneLake gives every Microsoft Fabric tenant a single, unified data lake built on open formats. One copy of data, many engines: that is the promise, and it is what makes OneLake such a strong foundation for analytics and AI alike. This post looks at how Sail , the open-source distributed compute framework, and LakeSail Cloud , the managed platform for running Sail in production, connect natively to OneLake, and what that unlocks for teams running Spark and Python workloads on Fabric. Sail is a drop-in replacement for Apache Spark, rebuilt from the ground up in Rust, with Rust-native support for Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg out of the box. That makes it a natural fit for OneLake, where lakehouse tables are stored in exactly these open formats. Point Sail at a Fabric lakehouse and it reads and writes the same tables the rest of Fabric uses, with no data copies, no extra connectors to install, and no changes to existing Spark code. One engine for data and AI Sail implements the Spark Connect protocol, the gRPC interface that decouples Spark clients from the engine that executes their plans. items.title: Simplify Teradata migrations with Fabric Migration Assistant (Preview)
items.excerpt: Migrating an enterprise Teradata estate to Microsoft Fabric can require extensive manual work across database objects, SQL and BTEQ code, dependencies, and operational processes. Fabric Migration Assistant helps reduce that effort so teams can focus their review on the objects and workflows that need attention. Fabric Migration Assistant for Data Warehouse now supports Teradata sources in preview. It converts eligible Teradata metadata and code to Fabric-compatible T-SQL, deploys eligible destination definitions, and flags scripts that need review or remediation, reducing the manual effort required to prepare a migration. You can choose which objects to migrate, review the translated code, and focus remediation on exceptions instead of manually translating every eligible object. Migration Assistant does not move the associated data; you load data in the following step of the migration flow. items.title: T-SQL language enhancements in Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse (Preview)
items.excerpt: Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse is expanding its T-SQL capabilities with four language enhancements in preview. GROUP BY ALL, ORDER BY ALL, the QUALIFY clause, and the FROM ... SELECT query format help SQL developers and data professionals reduce repetitive code, simplify query maintenance, and make analytical logic easier to understand. Figure: A T-SQL query uses GROUP BY ALL and ORDER BY ALL in Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse. What’s new Four T-SQL language enhancements are available in preview: GROUP BY ALL — automatically groups by every non-aggregate expression in the SELECT list, reducing duplication between SELECT and GROUP BY clauses. ORDER BY ALL — sorts results by each column in the SELECT list, using the same column order, so developers do not need to repeat every sort expression. QUALIFY — filters rows after window functions are evaluated, so common ranking and top-N patterns no longer require an additional subquery or common table expression. FROM ... SELECT — provides an alternative query format that begins with the data source and defines the selected columns later, allowing developers to write complex queries in a source-first sequence. Govern Skills are also now available in the Skills for Fabric collection, giving AI agents the knowledge they need to help admins and data owners audit, investigate, and remediate governance issues at scale. Both were announced at FabCon Europe 2026. Together, they help you monitor, manage, and act on your data estate from one place, whether you work in the Fabric portal or with an AI agent. Why it matters As AI makes it easier for more people to build with data, data estates grow in size and complexity. More workspaces, items, and access requests create more decisions about ownership, organization, and protection. Centralized, proactive governance helps admins support new projects without turning every decision into a manual review or losing visibility into how data is used. Governance can't rely on periodic, manual audits anymore. It needs to be proactive, centralized, and able to scale with the estate. items.title: Data Visualization in the Agentic Era
items.excerpt: Data visualizations help people identify patterns, trends, and outliers in their data. However, creating a useful visual requires several decisions: which chart and data to use, how to map the data to visual properties such as color and position, and how the finished visual should look. AI-assisted development can reduce that complexity by letting developers describe the intended result in natural language while reusable visualization components handle common design and interaction requirements. Deciding what visualization to create is one problem, while deciding how to create it is another. Power BI offers a convenient way to create reports and visualizations, but authors work within the chart types and formatting options that the product provides. AI coding agents another approach: developers can describe a visualization in natural language and optionally provide example images. Developers no longer have to start with a custom visual implementation or a visualization or graphics specification. Hello! But building real-time systems also requires teams to understand the events in motion, enriching them with business context, detecting and responding to any issues on time, and securely managing their streams across environments. That broader experience is the story behind this quarter’s updates. Eventstreams is expanding beyond connectivity and data movement to provide more of the capabilities teams need to work with streaming data after it arrives, while it is still in motion. With these expanded capabilities, users can now: Connect to more managed sources and extend Eventstreams with custom connectors. Capture change feeds from more operational databases. Explore and process multiple event types in a single Eventstream. Enrich streaming events with contextual data before processing and routing. Monitor processing health, diagnose problems, and act faster. Deploy with workspace-scoped networking and reusable configuration. items.title: Strengthening data security with workspace-level private connectivity for custom endpoints for Eventstream (Preview)
items.excerpt: Organizations that operate sensitive applications often keep them in networks with no route to the public internet. Applications in restricted networks need real-time analytics without a route to the public internet. Eventstream now supports workspace-level private links for custom endpoint sources (Preview), so those applications can send events to Microsoft Fabric over a private connection. Teams can bring sensitive operational data into real-time analytics without opening a public internet path for ingestion. The change is especially useful for in-house applications, services, and gateways that do not have a managed Eventstream connector. They can publish directly to a custom endpoint source through the workspace’s private connection, bringing these workloads into the same private networking model as supported connector-based sources. What is workspace-level private connectivity? Private Link is a network security feature of the Fabric platform that provides a private connection between a virtual network and Fabric.
